feed.title: TCP hole punching for Bitcoin nodes behind home NATs?

entry.title: TCP hole punching for Bitcoin nodes behind home NATs?
entry.summary:
The discussion at CoreDev Tokyo 2026 focused on the topic of TCP hole punching, specifically as it pertains to Bitcoin Core development. Participants explored techniques and challenges associated with enabling direct peer-to-peer connectivity in environments where nodes are positioned behind Network Address Translators (NATs). TCP hole punching was examined as a method to facilitate such connections without requiring manual port forwarding or relying on centralized servers.
Technical considerations highlighted included the intricacies of coordinating connection attempts between peers, handling various NAT behaviors, and the security implications of permitting unsolicited incoming connections. The conversation also addressed potential improvements to the existing peer discovery and connection mechanisms within Bitcoin Core, aiming to enhance network robustness and decentralization.
For further reference, the full transcript of the discussion is available at [https://btctranscripts.com/bitcoin-core-dev-tech/2026-10/tcp-hole-punching](https://btctranscripts.com/bitcoin-core-dev-tech/2026-10/tcp-hole-punching).
